decisions.reason: As a software-oriented add-on to the firm's established automation business, it is inexpensive to keep available and another year should reveal more demand from infrastructure operators.
The web-based dimensioning tool is likely very cheap to maintain, fits the firm's planner and engineering audience well, and remains a low-cost option worth keeping open.

The full fouling detection system probably ties up more support and implementation resources than a simple tool, but it matches the firm's efficiency-focused offering closely enough that management would wait for more market evidence.
Because this mechanically oriented product is still very new and municipal infrastructure sales cycles are long, management would keep the option open despite some risk that uptake may prove limited.

An energy management system fits the firm's stated strategic direction toward digitally networked, efficient, environmentally beneficial infrastructure, so it is worth retaining while adoption uncertainty resolves.
A dedicated product line with several models signals a stronger commercial commitment in a close-to-core application, making continued market presence the most likely choice.
